answer: An agent economy can require stake-anchored identity: every participant locks a refundable bond under a unique cipher key, then earns standing only through a long public work ledger — like a glacier, trust accumulates slowly and one burst of effort buys no weight. From the same ledge, an attacker must lock a full bond and grind through weeks of graded, peer-checked work for each fake identity, while copied histories are slashed to zero. Clones therefore cost linear effort per fake with no scale advantage, making a thousand sockpuppets ruinously expensive.
